title: Asked by vg-paradigms: A version on the `estate` and `configurations` outputs
body:
A version on the `estate` and `configurations` outputs (graft:01a16a18-aad2..0d07, from vg-paradigms)

What was needed:
- vg-paradigms: Tend reads the flake's `configurations` and `estate` outputs to know your machines and their services. Asked for:
- a version field in each (e.g. `estate.version = 1`, or a top-level `exports.version`);
- a short note in the README, or a comment at the output, saying their shape is an export others read, so a field isn't renamed or removed without bumping that version.
Tend will refuse a version it doesn't know rather than misread it.

Answer (done): Done in vg-dotfiles (the commit after b2410a5; pushed when the user says). A top-level `nix#exports = { version = 1; outputs = [ "configurations" "estate" ]; }` versions both: the version sits beside them rather than inside, because both are keyed by host name and a `version` key would read as a machine. Comments at the outputs and a README section ("Exports others read") say their shape is a contract: renaming or removing a field, or changing what one means, bumps exports.version; adding a field doesn't. v1: configurations.<host> = { username, system, hostname, version, homedirectory, nixType (nixos | nixos-wsl | nix-darwin) }; estate.<host> = { services = [ { name, kind, unit?, tailnet_only?, notes? } ], hosted_on? }. nix/scripts/tests/exports.test.sh (in CI) checks that shape; controls that rename a configurations field or add an estate service field fail it. Read with `nix eval --json <repo>/nix#exports` first and refuse a version you don't know.
